macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks finished the week lower as tech weakness returned
items.summary: U.S. equities ended the week down, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 snapping three-week winning streaks as investors refocused on Nvidia earnings and broader risk sentiment softened. Reports cited the S&P 500 down 1.5% and the Nasdaq down 2.5% for the week.

items.title: Major bond and rate expectations remain a market focus
items.summary: Markets continued to watch higher government bond yields, inflation pressures, and central-bank policy signals, with flash PMI data and upcoming inflation releases keeping rate expectations in play. One report said investors were awaiting additional clues from central banks, including the RBA and the Bank of Korea this week.

items.title: Fed inflation concerns and market sensitivity to policy remarks persisted
items.summary: A market recap cited Federal Reserve minutes that highlighted inflation concerns and discussion of rate hikes, while traders remained sensitive to shifting Treasury yields and risk appetite. The same coverage noted easing yields had supported stocks earlier, but policy uncertainty remained a dominant theme.

items.title: Nvidia earnings are the key company event driving sentiment
items.summary: Several market digests flagged Nvidia’s upcoming earnings report as the most important company catalyst for equities, with traders focused on positioning and whether the results can extend the AI-led rally. Separate reports also said Nvidia had warned some customers of price increases for certain AI servers.

items.title: Amazon raised prices on several devices
items.summary: Amazon increased prices overnight on several first-party products, including Echo, Fire TV, Kindle, and eero, according to a market news digest. The move added to attention on consumer-tech pricing and margin pressures.

items.title: Apple cut its standard EU App Store commission
items.summary: A financial newswire reported that Apple reduced its standard EU App Store commission from 30% to 26%. The change could affect app developer economics in the European market.

items.title: Canadian trade tensions escalated after new U.S. tariffs
items.summary: Canada-related coverage reported that the U.S. imposed 50% tariffs on selected Canadian imports after trade talks collapsed, with Ottawa planning retaliatory measures. The development added a fresh macro risk for North American trade and inflation sentiment.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major altcoins saw sharp 24-hour swings amid liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $77,300 and briefly approached $79,500 before pulling back, while related reports said the broader crypto market saw between about $995 million and $1.71 billion in liquidations over 24 hours. XRP, Ethereum, Solana, BNB, Cardano, and meme tokens also posted large intraday moves, reflecting elevated leverage-driven volatility.
items.source: Investing.com / Yahoo Finance / Coinglass via TradingView

items.title: Zcash hit an eight-year high after Grayscale advanced a U.S. trust plan
items.summary: Zcash surged more than 22% in 24 hours to about $819, extending a weekly rally above 30%. The move followed news that Grayscale advanced a U.S. Zcash trust effort, giving the privacy coin a major project-specific catalyst.

items.title: Bitcoin held above $77,000 after a Treasury-driven short squeeze
items.summary: Bitcoin traded just above $77,000 after reaching nearly $80,000, with traders attributing the move to U.S. Treasury buyback plans that boosted risk assets. Ether, XRP, Solana, BNB, Cardano, Dogecoin, and TRUMP also gained during the broader rally.

items.title: Cardano developers published an update roadmap for the Dijkstra upgrade
items.summary: Cardano developers released a schedule for the Dijkstra upgrade, which is intended to speed up transaction processing on the network. The rollout is planned in two phases, with the first expected by year-end and the second in Q2 2027.

items.title: U.S. Treasury released draft rules to implement the GENIUS Act for stablecoins
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury presented proposed rules for carrying out the GENIUS Act, the first federal law governing payment stablecoins. The draft outlines requirements for issuers, reserves, and oversight of dollar-backed stablecoins.

items.title: SEC reportedly introduced new crypto market rules, adding to regulatory focus
items.summary: A market report said the SEC presented new rules for the crypto market, contributing to the day’s regulatory news flow. The report did not provide full rule details, but it indicated continued U.S. policy attention on digital assets.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum rally broadened as crypto market cap jumped
items.summary: One market report said the crypto market rose nearly 8% in 24 hours to about $2.37 trillion, with Ethereum at one point up as much as 18% intraday. The move was linked to U.S. debt-market support headlines and stronger risk appetite.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI cuts GPT-5.6 Sol pricing as model competition intensifies
items.summary: OpenAI said it will lower benchmark pricing for GPT-5.6 Sol by more than 20% for developers, with the discount set to run for three months. The move comes amid broader price cuts across major AI model providers, including Google’s Gemini 3.7 Flash.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 3.7 Flash at a lower price point
items.summary: Google recently introduced Gemini 3.7 Flash and reduced its price to roughly half of the prior version, according to reporting on the latest model-price competition. The launch underscores a market shift toward cheaper frontier-model inference.

items.title: Nvidia-linked AI server costs rise as memory prices climb
items.summary: Reports say some Nvidia customers have been told AI server prices are rising by more than 15% because of higher memory-chip costs. The development points to inflationary pressure across the AI infrastructure supply chain.

items.title: Google’s Gemma model family reaches 1 billion downloads
items.summary: Google announced that the Gemma open-model family has surpassed 1 billion cumulative downloads, with more than 100,000 derivative models created by developers. The milestone highlights the scale of open-model adoption across edge, local, and specialized deployments.

items.title: Anthropic changes data-retention policy after enterprise pushback
items.summary: Industry roundup coverage says Anthropic updated its data-retention policy after pressure from enterprise users. The change reflects growing customer concern over privacy, governance, and how model providers handle business data.

items.title: OpenAI slows frontier model development over cybersecurity concerns
items.summary: A weekly big-tech AI roundup reports that OpenAI temporarily reduced the pace of frontier-model development due to rising cyber capability concerns. The same roundup says OpenAI is also emphasizing safer processing and zero-data-retention approaches for enterprise use.

items.title: Nvidia invests $6B with Poolside on US AI ecosystem buildout
items.summary: Nvidia reportedly committed $6 billion in a strategic partnership with Poolside to help build domestic AI computing infrastructure. The deal reflects continued heavy investment in compute capacity and AI ecosystem expansion.

items.title: AI infrastructure spending broadens beyond GPUs
items.summary: Recent AI investment reporting says the sector is moving from a GPU-only focus toward land, power, capital, and long-term supply contracts. Large compute-campus and infrastructure plans are increasingly central to competitive strategy.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Take-Two pursues legal action over GTA 6 leaks
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive has reportedly subpoenaed Microsoft and Discord as it tries to identify the source of recent Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leaks. Coverage says the company is seeking data tied to the accounts behind the leaks, while related reports indicate Rockstar and Take-Two remain unable to identify the person responsible.

items.title: Xbox said to be supporting Take-Two in GTA 6 leak investigation
items.summary: A report claims Xbox is assisting Take-Two’s effort to track down the leaker behind the recent GTA 6 footage. The same coverage says the game’s planned gameplay reveal and release date remain unchanged despite the leaks.

items.title: FromSoftware asks players not to share Duskbloods test footage
items.summary: FromSoftware has reportedly asked participants in the closed network test for The Duskbloods not to post or stream video and images from the test build. The request comes as the Switch 2 exclusive remains in development with no final release date confirmed.

items.title: The Duskbloods reportedly targets a 2026 launch on Switch 2
items.summary: Coverage around FromSoftware’s latest comments says The Duskbloods is still aiming for a 2026 release exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2. Another report notes that a briefly surfaced September 24 date was denied by Nintendo.

items.title: Gamescom chief says GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2 remain gaming’s 'north stars'
items.summary: Gamescom leadership highlighted Grand Theft Auto 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2 as hugely influential games in the industry. The same report also mentions that new GTA 6 leak material suggests the leaker may have had access to a playable build.

items.title: Gaming industry slowdown remains a major theme
items.summary: A market overview says the post-pandemic gaming boom has cooled, with major companies continuing layoffs, studio closures, and restructuring. It points to recent moves by EA, Microsoft, and Ubisoft as signs of a broader industry slowdown.

items.title: VGC reports on Nintendo’s anti-emulation crackdown
items.summary: VGC says Nintendo has removed hundreds more Switch emulator repositories from GitHub as part of its ongoing piracy enforcement effort. The report says seven additional emulators were taken down through DMCA requests.
